title: Your Mind Is the Market 🪞
hook: Clear the Mindset Mirror Lab, pass the Knowledge Check and save your Check-In to unlock Section 19.

game.title: Mindset Mirror Lab 🪞
game.tagline: Not “what is fear?”. Who is trading right now?
game.doneLine: You named the feeling, checked the market, read the rule, and chose the behavior. Over and over.

levels.thought: “I’m nervous this trade will come back.”

asks.prompt: DOES THAT THOUGHT ALONE REQUIRE AN ACTION?

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: No rule triggered and nothing changed in price.

options.label: No
options.why: No action is required solely from that thought.

levels.name: Feeling or rule?
levels.brief: Who is trading right now? Recognize yourself in the decision.

levels.thought: “I don’t want to lose the green.”

who.why: FEAR-DRIVEN MANAGEMENT: protecting unrealized profit by abandoning the plan.

rule.text: Fixed management: hold to SL −30 / TP +60.

levels.name: The green

fallback.line: A very common one: entering after the planned retest is already gone.

who.why: FOMO / CHASE. The planned entry was the retest. Price leaving doesn’t create a new one.

market.state: ICC complete · no retest · price +20 away

who.why: GREED / PLAN DRIFT: no runner rule, the management model changed because of excitement.
REVENGE: would she take this exact setup if the previous trade never happened? No.

options.label: Take it, small
options.feedback: Small is still a third trade.

who.why: Mediocre + “it’s something” = activity looking for a reason.

asks.prompt: SCENARIO A: Continuation hasn’t closed yet. She waits.

options.label: HESITATION
options.feedback: The criteria aren’t complete. Waiting is the model.

asks.prompt: SCENARIO B: Full valid setup, first retest, risk valid, the session allows it. She skips it only because her last trade lost.

options.label: PATIENCE
options.feedback: Everything was complete. She waited AFTER the criteria.

options.label: HESITATION / FEAR
options.why: Criteria complete, rules allow it: the previous trade is deciding.

asks.prompt: Five wins in a row. Proposed: triple size on the next trade. DID THE RISK MODEL CHANGE?

options.label: Yes, she earned it
options.feedback: Wins don’t change the risk model. They change how it feels.

options.label: NO
options.why: Same baseline: 1R. Confidence changed. Risk didn’t disappear.

asks.prompt: Two valid losses today, both executed by the rules. “ICC stopped working.” What’s the process response?

options.label: Rewrite the method tonight
options.feedback: Two trades isn’t a sample. Judge the strategy slowly.

options.label: Review execution + the sample
options.why: Behavior: judged quickly (followed ✓). Strategy: judged slowly, across a meaningful sample.

options.label: Skip the next valid setup
options.feedback: That’s hesitation dressed up as caution.

trades.name: THE TRADE
trades.why: Crucial: the journal stores WIN and RULE VIOLATION side by side. The win doesn’t erase it.

asks.prompt: A valid setup begins forming. DOES THIS EMOTIONAL STATE MAKE THE MARKET SETUP INVALID?

options.label: YES
options.feedback: The setup is price. The state is her. Different dimensions.

options.label: NO
options.why: Trader readiness and setup validity are separate.

asks.prompt: DOES YOUR PERSONAL TRADING PLAN NEED A RULE FOR WHAT YOU DO IN THIS STATE?

options.label: YES
options.why: Don’t invent it now. Section 2 is where you build it.

options.label: NO
options.feedback: Then live-trading-you decides. In a red state. 😭

levels.title: One continuous session

options.label: Get it back on the next one
LOG IT. Continue only if the plan permits.
options.why: A valid loss is logged, not avenged.

end.card: The market moved without your entry. That’s all.

events.title: Trade 3 · valid, and you feel hesitant

asks.prompt: Valid setup forming. Risk valid. Daily rules permit. You feel hesitant after the loss and the miss. WHAT SHOULD DETERMINE THE DECISION?

options.label: How I feel right now
options.feedback: Notice it. Don’t let it decide.

options.label: CURRENT SETUP + CURRENT RULES
options.why: Not the previous trade. Not the feeling. The setup and the rules.

events.title: Event 4 · the cleanest setup of the day

checkpoints.prompt: The cleanest setup of the session. Your daily stop is reached.

end.text: It went on to win. Without you.
end.card: THE CORRECT DECISION CAN MISS MONEY.

levels.reviewClean: You felt the loss, the miss and the hesitation. None of them got to rewrite the model.
levels.name: FINAL BOSS: Who is trading right now?

questionBank.question: She feels nervous. The plan and the market are unchanged. What does the feeling require?
options: Nothing by itself: feeling ≠ required action
questionBank.why: A feeling is information. With no rule triggered and nothing changed, no action is required.

questionBank.question: Valid setup, risk valid, session rules allow it. She skips it only because her previous trade lost. What is it?
questionBank.why: Waiting AFTER the criteria are complete is hesitation.

questionBank.question: Continuation hasn’t closed. She waits. What is it?
questionBank.why: Waiting FOR the criteria is patience.

questionBank.question: No retest. Price runs. She enters late. What is it?
questionBank.why: The planned entry was the retest. Entering late is a chase.

questionBank.question: No retest. Price runs all the way to the target. She does nothing. How do you grade it?
questionBank.why: No retest, no chase. A missed profit isn’t a loss.

questionBank.question: She loses −1R. The next setup is incomplete. She sizes up to recover. What is it?
questionBank.why: Urgency to repair the last outcome plus unauthorized size.

questionBank.question: Five wins in a row. She doubles size because she feels “locked in.” What is it?
questionBank.why: Confidence changed. The risk model didn’t.

questionBank.question: She hits +2R. Her predefined plan includes runner management, and she follows it. Is that greed?
questionBank.why: A planned runner is the plan working.

questionBank.question: Her plan allows up to four trades. Trade 3 meets her full criteria. Is it overtrading?
questionBank.why: Overtrading is trading beyond YOUR plan.

questionBank.question: A trade wins after she violated her entry rule. How is it journaled?
questionBank.why: Outcome and process are separate. A win doesn’t erase a violation.

questionBank.question: A trade loses after perfect execution. How is it journaled?
questionBank.why: A valid loss is not a bad trade.

questionBank.question: One loss and she concludes the strategy is broken. What’s wrong with that?
questionBank.why: Judge behavior quickly. Judge the strategy slowly, over a meaningful sample.

questionBank.question: She moved to break even at +26 with no break-even rule. What most likely changed the plan?
questionBank.why: No rule triggered and structure didn’t change. Fear did.

questionBank.question: She’s in a red revenge state as a valid setup forms. What’s true?
options: The setup can still be valid; her personal rule for this state matters
She must take it to get back to calm
Emotion and setup are the same thing
questionBank.why: Setup validity and trader readiness are different dimensions.
